On my Top 10 List of U.S. Cuban Restos!
Mar 2026 • Family
Being Cuban American, I am a real super Foodie when it comes to traditional, tasty, unique and well-prepared Cuban Cuisine. And Versailles Restaurant is one of those few places left in Florida, especially Miami, that you can still satisfy the craving of one’s heritage at one sitting, with a multitude of dishes on the menu. This is a unique restaurant in its own right and it’s not just because of its fabulous food, but it’s like walking into another world. Versailles is an enormous multi room establishment that mixes French aesthetics with ornate mirrors, chandeliers and the like with Cuban cultural styles to create a unique, intriguing and comfortable atmosphere. They do serve traditional breakfast and one of my faves, the Omelet Sandwich! It’s a place you can frequent for snacks, big meals, sammiches or just into their “Ventanita” por un Cafecito or Dulce. If you enjoy coffee, don’t forget to order the Café Cubano or El Cortadito. Appetizing, perfectly presented and delish traditional meals include: Vaca Frita. A shredded beef perfectly grilled up with onions and Cuban Mojo that’s served with Moros y Cristianos (mixed black beans and white rice) and sided with sweet plantains; one of my faves since childhood, Tasajo is shredded dried beef cooked with lotsa onions, Bell peppers, tomato sauce and wine then served with white rice and fried sweet potato; then the world famous Boliche (Cuban Pot Roast) articulated in the perfectly prepared roasted Eye Round beef stuffed with Spanish sausage and cooked in garlic, with onions, Bell peppers, lots of yummy Cuban spices and wine and offered with Moros y Cristianos and Sweet Plantains; another fave includes braised Oxtails that are rendered with traditional Cuban spices in a Red Wine Sauce and served with White Rice and Sweet Plantains. For the Fish and Seafood lover is the Zarzuela De Mariscos which compiles sautéed lobster, shrimp, squid, clams, mussels and fish with olive oil, garlic, onion, Bell pepper in a marinated tomato sauce and served with white rice and nice and sweet plantains. They also offer some traditional sandwiches like the fab Croquette Sandwich consisting of sweet ham, Swiss cheese on Cuban Bread. Then there is the King of Sammiches, the Cuban Sandwich with sweet ham, roast pork, Swiss cheese on a toasted Cuban bread with mustard and pickles – all prepared with Mojo Criollo. They also offer one of the most misunderstood Cuban dishes, that of Fufú de Platanos (mashed green plantains). It’s a traditional Cuban of boiled and mashed plátanos with Criollo mix of garlic, lard, chicken stock, along with salt and pepper – may not sound or look appetizing, but you’ll see! Then there is the Paella Valenciana made with Lobster, shrimp, squid, mussels, chicken and fish, over rice and saffron. And my all-time fave, that simple Liver Sauté prepared with thick strips sautéed with caramelized onions, Bell pepper and wine and served with white rice and sweet plantains. The list goes on and on. I’ve been eating here for over fifty years, and all along they’ve been consistent, friendly, quality-centric, and satisfying in both taste and tradition. South Florida has a myriad and uncountable array of “Cuban” restos, from traditional to nouvelle, but to me, Versailles is within my top 5 locally family-owned establishments that offer the real deal! With every visit to my home town, comes a visit to Versailles… my hometown kitchen depended on since my Grandma passed! I highly recommend this incredibly unique eatery I have visited since my high school days – thank you Felipe Valls Sr., Founder, for creating and keeping heritage, tradition, nostalgia and great food as the utmost of importance! Buen provecho!

When in Miami, have some great Cuban food. This restaurant was right down the street from where we were staying. A quick internet search told us we should go there and according to their website, they are ‘known as the World’s Most Famous Cuban Restaurant’. It’s 9:30 pm and we managed to find a parking place, then had to wait for a table. 9:30 pm and we had to wait. There’s a large patio area with a bar and people waiting were enjoying some of their favorite cocktails. We walked through this large establishment just to check it out. We found a take out counter that was doing a brisk business. Then there’s the bakery. Everything looked good and they too were busy. We sat back out on the patio and were seated in maybe 15 minutes. As it was late, we wanted something, but not too heavy. We ordered a Cubana Especial ($13.75), which is a larger size of the regular Cuban Sandwich, and one Tamal en Hoja ($4.25), which is a tamale wrapped in corn husk. The sandwich was a true authentic Cuban. Cuban bread, soft inside, toasted and pressed with ham, roast pork, Swiss cheese, mustard and pickle. It was great. The tamale was tasty, like most tamales. I had a Hatuey Cuban Style Lager ($7.00/ bottle) which was a little different than our typical US lagers. Perfectly enjoyable. People bear us really enjoyed the Mojitos. We saw so many great dishes go past us, but we’ll have to wait for a return visit to try more. Now we know why it was so busy. Give them a try.

Jun 2026 • Family
My first visit to Versailles Restaurant ,many people labeled Versailles as a classic must visit spot in Miami 5/5 Stars (Nostalgia) for the "best cuban cuisine in the area" my visit was unfortunately disappointing.
The wait time was reasonable for such a popular restaurant. We were told it would be about a 50-minute wait, but we were seated in roughly 35 minutes, which was a pleasant surprise. One thing I did notice, however, was that the check-in process seemed inefficient. There was one lady at the front, with a wonderful Cuban accent, doing her best to call out names, but many guests weren't paying attention or responding. It appeared to make her job much more difficult and likely slowed the process down. I genuinely felt for her and made sure to thank her when we were finally seated.
For the appetizers we ordered the croquetas variadas: jamon (ham) pollo (chicken)and bacallao (fish)
Croquetas are an acquired taste, I personally thought these taste it like a can of deviled ham that was deep fried and wasn't very tasty at all and felt like mush as I ate them but apparently this is a very popular thing in Cuban Cuisine 1/5 Stars..no thanks moving on
For my meal, I ordered the Arroz con Pollo. While it had some flavor, it was extremely dry and honestly one of the least enjoyable versions of the dish I've ever had. The presentation looked rushed, as if the ingredients had simply been thrown together and plopped on a plate. It arrived so quickly i felt it had been sitting pre-made and waiting to be served. Unfortunately, it did not make a good first impression. 2/5 Stars
My wife ordered the Vaca Frita, which was also disappointing. The meat didn't taste particularly fresh and had an odd texture--crunchy both on the outside and inside. It was lightly seasoned and lacked the bold flavors we expected from traditional Cuban cuisine.2/5 Stars
Overall, our experience left us confused For a restaurant with such a strong reputation, we expected food that reflected the care, tradition, and authenticity Cuban cuisine is known for. Instead, it felt more like plates were being pushed out as quickly as possible to keep up with demand.
 Overall 3/5 Stars and Versailles has given me no reason to go back on my next visit to Miami.

Mar 2026 • Family
We have been wanting to have lunch here for a long time and finally made it last Monday. We wanted to avoid the huge crowds so we got here around 1130am. There were no lines and we lucked out parking very close to the front door. We were seated right away near the front and were served immediately. Versailles is a very large restaurant with French inspired ornate mirrors and lovely chandeliers. It is known as "The World's Most Famous Cuban Restaurant," attracting locals, tourists, celebrities, and politicians. It should be a must visit on your list. We are very happy that we went!

Our food was delicious!! My daughter had her Cuban favorite, Vaca de Frita, and loved it. Generous portions here, by the way. I ordered the Lechon Asado (roast pork) with rice & black beans and boiled yucca, which was to die for!! I can't wait to go back for this meal again. We both had cafe con leche, but it wasn't what we hoped for unfortunately. I would get a cortadito next time. For dessert, she got the Tres Leches and I got the Guava and cheese pie. Besides the restaurant, there is a Cuban bakery inside with delicious pastries and cakes. The La Ventanita is their coffee shop window outside attached to their building. Take a nunber. There is plentiful parking. Indoor and outdoor seating.

Our server, Yudiel, was excellent. He was friendly, attentive, graciously explained the menu questions we had, and checked on us several times even though it had become very busy by then. We appreciated his service. We look forward to returning very soon.

THIS is where Cubans and others can definitely come and enjoy a little piece of Cuba. The Take Out area was like a family gathering. Many posted at the Window eating a variety of Empanadas that you are able to order. From a moussed ham and cheese, chopped beef and olives and chicken. Loved the beef and chicken. The ham's texture was something to be desired but the flavor was good!
The Mojitos are A MUST!!!! Especially the Mango and Guava with fresh mint and Cane sugar stick. 
The Yuca Fries were piping hot, crispy on the outside and pillowy on the inside. The savory Mojo sauce was just right. 
The Arroz Con Pollo were two juicy pieces of a leg and thigh, buried underneath flavored and Veggie packed yellow rice. It came with Peas and minced red peppers with Cilantro. Unfortunately, the rice is cooked separately and was lukewarm but the chicken was piping hot. 
The room temperature rice was similar for the Roasted Pork dish. We swapped white for yellow rice. The Frijoles Negro were fresh and a good accompaniment. The Roast Pork was seasoned with great salinity and vinegar. Needed more onions and better served parts but the Chicharron was a crunchy and salty piece of amazing!
Also got a Cubano to go. Almost got as a main but our waitperson said, NO, get the Roast Pork and wisely so! The Cubano was perfect for a late night bite. Of course it was made with the same Lechon. 
No room for dessert. 
It STAYS packed! The Service is swift, personable and efficient. They get you in, well fed and out. If you have to wait, you can order drinks. 
Plenty of parking and they have their own large lot. 
Versailles is a Miami treasure and MUST for a DELICIOUS REASON!!!!
